hints.title: In-Place Targeted Value Removal Obstacle
hints.text: Repeatedly deleting matching values causes quadratic time due to repeated element shifting. How can you scan the collection once and move all non-matching numbers to the front using constant extra space?

hints.title: Compaction Pointer Invariant
hints.text: Keep a pointer marking the boundary of retained items. Each time an element not equal to the target value is found, copy it to the boundary index and step forward.

hints.title: Linear Scan Filtering Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a write index k to zero. Iterate an index i through the entire array. If the value at index i does not equal the forbidden value, copy it to index k and increment k. Once the loop finishes, return k as the new length.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (0 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Single pass in-place filtering with constant auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Calling remove() or erase() on matching elements shifts all subsequent elements to the left, taking O(N) per deletion and O(N^2) total time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Overwriting elements in-place avoids extra memory allocation while preserving linear O(N) runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling arrays with zero matches or all matches cleanly, modifying the input array in-place, and returning the count k.
